notes: Only the seven advertised tools in the prompt were judged. n8n management tools present in the source were not included because they were not in the advertised tool list.

All advertised tools here are READ under the enforcement definition; none of them writes state, executes host code, or sends agent-supplied data to an attacker-chosen destination in the cited code paths.

get_node.rationale: `get_node` reads node records by caller-supplied `nodeType` and returns stored documentation/schema fields such as `node.documentation`. The advertised modes can also include real-world template examples. Because the database includes community nodes/templates, node documentation, names, property descriptions, and examples may be authored by third parties; these returned fields are UNTRUSTED. There is no write or agent-chosen network destination in this code path.

get_template.rationale: `get_template` retrieves public workflow templates by `templateId` from the template service and returns template information plus workflow JSON. Public/community templates contain author-controlled names, descriptions, workflow node names, parameters, notes, and other text, so the output is UNTRUSTED. It is a read-only local retrieval and has no agent-chosen network destination.

search_nodes.rationale: `search_nodes` searches the node database and can include community nodes and community/template examples. The docs state searches include community nodes and return community metadata such as `authorName`; README also describes community nodes. Community registry/package metadata and public template examples are third-party/public content, so returned node metadata/examples are attacker-controllable under the threat model. It does not contact an agent-chosen host or write state.

search_templates.rationale: `search_templates` searches public/community workflow templates in several modes and returns template records or mined pattern summaries. The documented return fields include `name`, `description`, `author`, `url`, `metadata`, and pattern data derived from templates; these are public multi-writer/template-library content and can be attacker-authored. It does not write state or contact an agent-chosen host.

tools_documentation.rationale: `tools_documentation` is a read-only static documentation lookup: `executeTool` dispatches to `getToolsDocumentation`, which returns either `getToolsOverview` or `getToolDocumentation`. The returned content is built from packaged documentation objects, not from user accounts, arbitrary URLs, or public multi-writer content.

validate_node.rationale: `validate_node` is read-only validation, but it looks up node definitions and returns fields such as `displayName` and missing required property names from the node database. For community nodes those node/property names and related validation text can be third-party-authored. It does not write state or send data to an agent-chosen destination.

validate_workflow.rationale: `validate_workflow` is read-only validation, but its output includes validation `errors`, `warnings`, node names, details, and suggestions for the caller-supplied workflow. When the workflow comes from public templates or other third-party sources, those node names and text incorporated into diagnostics can be attacker-controlled. The tool does not write state or send data to an agent-chosen destination.

value_conditions.effect: If a requested tool name is present in `DISABLED_TOOLS`, `executeTool` rejects the call; by default no tools are disabled by this check.

For `search_nodes`, restricting `source` to core nodes and not requesting template examples removes the community-node/template-example sources of the UNTRUSTED label for that call; default is `source: "all"` and `includeExamples: false`.

For `get_node`, using only core node types and not requesting template examples avoids community/template-authored output for that call; default `includeExamples` is false, but `nodeType` is caller-selected and may name community nodes.
value_conditions.syntax: get_node arguments selecting only trusted core node types and includeExamples=false
